title: The Picnic
strapline: Pack the basket, spread the blanket, share it round — eating together, outdoors, on purpose.
intent: A picnic is a whole, warm sequence children can own — planning, packing, carrying, spreading out and sharing — with eating together as the sociable heart.
Deciding what to pack and sharing it fairly around the blanket invites planning, counting and generous turn-taking.
Packing and unpacking a basket is a satisfying spatial puzzle, and carrying it outdoors is real, purposeful physical work.
The relaxed, side-by-side nature of a picnic draws children into easy conversation about food, weather and each other.
A picnic welcomes the foods every family packs, so it becomes a place to share and celebrate different tastes and customs.
Whether real snack or pretend feast, the picnic connects children to eating outdoors and to simple ideas of preparing for an outing.
implementation: Plan the picnic together — what shall we take, how many are coming, what will we need to carry it?
Provide a real basket, blanket, plates and cups (and real snack when you can) so packing, carrying and sharing all mean something.
Make the sharing genuine: 'five friends on the blanket, how do we share these four sandwiches fairly?'
Take the play outdoors whenever weather allows, and let children choose the spot and spread the blanket themselves.
Invite families to suggest or send a picnic food from their own table, and name and celebrate each one.
Talk about the weather and preparing for it — 'do we need sun hats, or a coat in case it rains?'
key_questions: What shall we take, and how many are coming?
Five friends on the blanket — how do we share four sandwiches fairly?
How will we carry everything we need?
Do we need sun hats, or a coat in case it rains?
What picnic food does your family like to pack?
